title: Chocolate Layer Cake
summary: A moist, deeply chocolatey layer cake made with an oil-based batter and coffee for extra depth, finished with glossy chocolate ganache.
equipment: two 20 cm round cake tins (5 cm deep), greased and base-lined
stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: hot strong coffee or boiling water
ingredients.note: coffee deepens the chocolate; it is not tasted

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (about 60% cocoa solids), finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat the Oven
steps.text: Set the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) and let it heat for at least 20 minutes before baking, with a shelf positioned in the middle.

steps.title: Bloom the Cocoa
steps.text: Whisk the cocoa powder into the hot coffee until smooth, then leave it for 5 minutes. Blooming cocoa in hot liquid like this draws out more of its flavour than simply stirring it into the batter dry.

steps.title: Mix Wet and Dry Separately
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, bicarbonate of soda, baking powder and salt together in a large bowl. In a second bowl, whisk the oil, eggs, buttermilk and vanilla, then whisk in the cocoa mixture.

steps.title: Combine the Batter
steps.text: Pour the wet mixture into the dry and whisk just until smooth; the batter will be noticeably thin, which is normal for this style of cake. Overmixing here is the main way to end up with a tough, rubbery crumb instead of a moist one.

steps.title: Bake the Layers
steps.text: Divide the batter between the two tins and bake for 30-35 minutes, until the tops spring back to the touch and a skewer comes out with just a few moist crumbs clinging to it.

steps.title: Cool Completely
steps.text: Cool the cakes in their tins for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and leave to cool fully before icing.

steps.title: Make the Ganache
steps.text: Bring the cream just to the boil and pour it over the chopped chocolate. Leave for 3 minutes, then stir from the centre outwards until glossy and smooth, before stirring in the butter and salt.

steps.title: Thicken the Ganache
steps.text: Leave the ganache at room temperature for 1-1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until it's thick enough to spread, holding its shape rather like soft peanut butter. Whip it for 30 seconds with the mixer if you'd like a lighter, fluffier frosting.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Sandwich the cooled layers with a third of the ganache, then spread the remainder over the top and sides to finish.

tips: Don't skip the coffee bloom - it isn't there for a coffee flavour, just to make the chocolate taste richer.
The batter is meant to be thin; resist adding more flour, as it will bake up moist rather than dense.
Let the ganache cool and thicken properly before spreading - using it warm will just slide off the sides of the cake.
Make sure the cakes are completely cool before assembling, or the ganache will melt and pool.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 2 days, or in the fridge for up to 5 days, bringing slices back to room temperature before serving. The unfrosted sponges freeze well, wrapped tightly, for up to 2 months.
